solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Not much money for battery charger? (11)

blocks.note: a battery hen 'charges' at its grain: the food meant for poultry

annotation.surface: Someone grumbling that a phone charger costs next to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Battery charger' looks like a gadget for phones; read it as a hen in a battery farm, where hens are kept in rows of small cages. Her grain doubles as a paltry sum.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: poultry grain is cheap, so the phrase came to mean a trifling amount of money.

indicators.note: a short form of the word: its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: KERB, the roadside edge, loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A rambler saying hello to someone at the edge of the road.
annotation.walkthrough: Kerb is the British spelling of curb, the raised edge of the pavement beside the road.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anyone out walking the hills for pleasure.

annotation.surface: A drawback of mixing ingredients inside a puzzle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' sits at the end looking like a noun; it is the verb, to baffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to baffle or bewilder someone.

entries.clue: Festival where gourmand absorbs sugar, primarily (6)

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it in, so the eater takes the letter inside
take the first letter of 'sugar'

blocks.note: a gourmand is a big eater

annotation.surface: A feast day on which a glutton puts away sweets.
annotation.walkthrough: The chocolate eggs make the surface fit the answer neatly, which hides the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Christian spring feast is one festival among many.

entries.clue: In favour of having revised since describing investigative science (8)

indicators.note: the letters of 'since' are reworked into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone backing a theory, having rethought it since learning about crime-lab science.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase: the answer is the word describing the science of crime investigation.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective for science applied to criminal investigation.

entries.clue: Make a peer raise the Spanish hat briefly (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upwards, so it reads backwards
cut short: BONNET loses its last letter

annotation.surface: An instruction to lift a Spanish hat, perhaps in honour of a new lord.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole of ELBONNE is read upwards. A peer is a member of the British nobility, such as a duke or baron.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb phrase: to raise someone to the peerage.

blocks.note: in the concessive sense: nevertheless, however

annotation.walkthrough: Two words that look unrelated, but and together, both lead to the same phrase: one in its concessive sense, one in its timing sense.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'nevertheless' and 'simultaneously'.

indicators.note: done hastily and carelessly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

annotation.surface: A thrill-seeker has acted on impulse again.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the pleasure-seeker is what 'done this' rashly makes. The surface fits the answer, which is what makes it hard to split.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who lives for pleasure above all else.

blocks.note: what you are doing when on the floor

annotation.surface: Someone rolling about on the floor in fits of laughter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Laughing' is the colloquial sense: if you have it made, you're laughing. The surface wants it to mean helpless mirth.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both mean being comfortably placed, with nothing to worry about.

indicators.note: about means around, so the number goes around the other piece

annotation.surface: A figure deemed correct for a gift voucher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' is often ten, and 'right' can be OK as well as R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a book token exchanged for goods.

indicators.note: decorating rearranges things, here the letters

annotation.surface: Simple entries, for example, used to adorn something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plain' passes for an adjective meaning simple; it is the noun, a flat grassland.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Tanzanian grassland is one particular plain.

entries.clue: Very difficult cryptic clue ran on gas (9)

indicators.note: made mysterious, so the letters are scrambled
in an across clue, one thing 'on' another comes after it, so the anagram follows HE

annotation.surface: A fiendish crossword clue that went on and on about gas.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a solver's complaint, and 'cryptic clue' reads as a single phrase; split it, and 'cryptic' is the instruction on 'clue ran'.
annotation.definitionFit: Named after the twelve labours of the Greek hero, it describes any enormously hard task.

entries.clue: Great help fitting heel of actress into footwear (5)

indicators.note: the heel is the back end, so the last letter
the letter goes inside the footwear

annotation.surface: A stylist helping an actress squeeze her foot into a shoe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heel' and 'footwear' keep the surface in the shoe shop, disguising heel as a letter-position word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a lift or shot in the arm that helps a great deal.

blocks.note: a sac is a bag-like container

annotation.surface: A vessel of wine that has been blessed, as at communion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Container' looks like a mechanism word; here it is just a sac.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something consecrated and holy has been blessed.

entries.clue: Epic duos, when dancing, became intimate (6,2)

indicators.note: letters that dance move about into a new order

annotation.surface: Famous dance partnerships growing close on the ballroom floor.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a gossip line about dance partners, which is exactly what the answer says.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to snuggle close and become intimate.

indicators.note: to wind (rhymes with 'find') is to twist, so the letters are twisted round

annotation.surface: A freezing gale blowing through Serbia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as a gust, with 'Very cold' describing it; it is the verb that rhymes with find.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative use: the Russian region's winters make its adjective a byword for bitter cold.

annotation.surface: A wiring fault that could injure someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like the verb of possibility; it is the noun, strength. The answer is the British term for a blackout.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a loss of the electricity supply is one electrical problem.

entries.clue: Balloon in space to which sentimentality gets attributed (8)

blocks.note: room = space; the mush is 'attributed' to it, set in front

annotation.surface: A balloon floating in a room gushing with sentiment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Balloon' is the verb, to swell rapidly. The long phrase just says the sentimentality is attached to the space.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: both mean to expand fast.

entries.clue: Dish is too much when stuck in middle of throat (7)

indicators.note: the pieces are lodged inside
take the central letters of 'throat'

blocks.note: the middle two letters of thROat

annotation.surface: A meal that is too big to swallow, lodged halfway down.
annotation.walkthrough: OTT, short for 'over the top', is the standard abbreviation for too much.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Italian rice dish is one kind of dish.

indicators.note: the shed has the other word placed around it

annotation.surface: A garden shed with a swallow wheeling round it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: closed up and locked, as a house for the winter.

entries.clue: American city enthusiastic about welcoming American (7)

blocks.note: US = American, taken in (welcomed) by HOT

annotation.surface: A US city keen on receiving a fellow American.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot on' is a set phrase for keen about, and the clue splits it round a second 'American'. The first 'American' belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Texas city is one American city.

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper

annotation.surface: A method recorded on paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective, up to date; it is the flow of water.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a flow of water is a current.

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken
the hidden letters are read backwards

annotation.surface: A hairdresser cutting back some hair.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a salon visit, and 'trimmed' looks like the deletion instruction; it only supplies the T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long lock of hair.

entries.clue: Retinue of attendants, ten surprisingly born when we were? (9)

indicators.note: the letters of ten turn up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: people born when we were are of OUR AGE

annotation.surface: A band of followers who, surprisingly, are exactly our age.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose phrase: those born when we were are our age.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the group of attendants around someone important.

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so GEN goes inside AT
the essence of 'data', its middle letters

blocks.note: the middle two letters of dATa

annotation.surface: Key facts found at the heart of a data set.
annotation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who acts on another's behalf.

entries.clue: Hairy growth touches man when cut off (9)

indicators.note: hairy = wild, chaotic, so the letters are jumbled
a word cut off is docked at its end, so MAN loses its N

blocks.note: MAN with its last letter cut off

annotation.surface: A man shaving off the whiskers he keeps touching.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hairy growth' reads as one phrase and a full definition; 'Hairy' is really the anagram instruction, meaning wild.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: hair on the upper lip is one kind of growth.

annotation.surface: Gossip picked up from 'a little bird told me'.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'a little bird told me'; the bird's chirp and the social-media post are one word.
annotation.definitionFit: Covers a short online message and a bird's chirp.

entries.clue: Poison bear consuming last of venom ingested (11)

indicators.note: CONTAIN eats the M, taking it inside
take the final letter of 'venom'

annotation.surface: A bear that has swallowed venom and is poisoned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb, to hold.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to make impure, as a toxin does a water supply.
